name: Citation Auditing and Good Law Checking
title: Citation Auditing and Good Law Checking
answer: Citation auditing and good law checking is the practice of verifying that every authority cited in a legal document exists, says what it is claimed to say, and remains valid. It covers citation format, pin cites, quotations, parentheticals, jurisdiction, court level, precedential status, and subsequent history such as reversal, overruling, amendment, or negative treatment. In AI law, the site tracks 29 AI case law precedents, and each one needs the same good law checks as any other authority. The work also includes checking that cited statutes, regulations, and secondary sources have not been superseded. It is distinct from legal research on the merits, though the two often overlap.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Citation auditing runs on the same legal research infrastructure as ordinary case law research: citators, full text databases, court dockets, and the documents under review. Well known citators such as Shepard's and KeyCite provide treatment signals, while Westlaw, LexisNexis, and free sources such as CourtListener provide text and metadata. AI assisted systems add citation extraction, entity resolution, retrieval, and comparison against source documents. The infrastructure also includes word processing files, PDFs, and briefs that need to be parsed into individual citations. For AI law specifically, teams may maintain internal indexes of AI related opinions and regulatory materials to catch new developments.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work usually starts with extracting every citation from a draft or filed document, then normalizing each one to a standard reporter citation. A researcher then checks the citation in a citator for subsequent history and negative treatment, reads the cited passage in context, and confirms that the proposition it supports is accurate. For quotations, the checker compares the exact words and pin cite against the source. AI tools can speed up extraction and flag mismatches, but a human reviewer typically resolves ambiguous citations and judgment calls about precedential weight. The output is a citation audit memo or a marked up draft with corrections and open questions.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Citation auditing carries professional responsibility risks because courts and bar authorities expect filings to be accurate and supported. Sanctions, reputational harm, and client harm can follow from citing a case that has been overruled or misquoted. Provenance matters: each citation is traced to a reliable source, and AI generated citations are verified against the original opinion or statute rather than accepted from a model output. Data rights and licensing also apply when using commercial citators and databases, so teams track what content they can store, share, or feed into other systems. Confidentiality rules may limit how draft documents and client facts are handled in third party tools.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Citation auditing is moving toward more automated extraction, graph based treatment analysis, and continuous monitoring of cited authorities. As AI related litigation grows, new opinions will enter the citator ecosystem and require good law checks. Courts are also issuing standing orders and local rules about AI use in filings, which changes how audits are documented. Better retrieval and citation grounding may reduce hallucinated references, but the final judgment about whether a case is good law remains a human and professional call. The likely direction is tighter integration between drafting tools, citators, and audit trails that record when and how each citation was checked.
